stories.title: Austria's Leipzig drone accusations against Russia show it is not neutral — embassy
stories.summary: The Russian side has rejected baseless accusations, which lack any proof, material evidence or solid argumentation, the embassy stressed
article_sentences: By jumping on the anti-Russia bandwagon and accusing Moscow of being behind the Leipzig/Halle Airport drone incident, Austria proved once again that it is not a neutral actor, the Russian embassy in Vienna said in a statement.
The embassy drew attention to Austrian Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger’s statement.

According to the diplomatic mission, it contains "harsh condemnation" of Russia and accusations of a "hybrid attack on Leipzig." "It is disappointing that Austria, forgetting once again its declared neutral status, has joined the EU anti·Russian narrative and deliberately chosen to worsen bilateral relations," the statement posted on the embassy’s Telegram channel reads.
The Russian side has rejected baseless accusations, which lack any proof, material evidence or solid argumentation, the embassy stressed.
The diplomatic mission added that Austria has expressed solidarity with Germany and called for new anti·Russian sanctions.
"The summoning of the Russian ambassador to the Austrian Foreign Ministry has been announced in advance," the embassy noted.

stories.title: 'Glacier melt and sea level rise will continue: We cannot leave this to the next generation'
stories.summary: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Inger Andersen, Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations and Executive Director of the United Nations Environment Programme. Her central argument is that decades of what she calls “carbon procrastination” have made exceeding 1.5°C unavoidable: the question is therefore no longer simply whether the world crosses 1.5°C, but by how much, for how long, and with what consequences for vulnerable societies and ecosystems. While mitigation remains essential, adaptation becomes equally important as sea-level rise and glacier loss, will continue even as emissions fall.

stories.title: Beastie Boy Mike D releases his first solo LP 'Thank You'
stories.summary: Mike D rose to fame in the 1980s as part of New York's Beastie Boys, a rap-rock trio who soon tired of poking fun at frat boy humour with hits like "Fight for Your Right (To Party!)" and" Girls". The band quickly moved on thanks to their passion for beat making, sampling and playing around in the studio, establishing themselves over three decades as credible genre-bending musicians.
